newsitem.title: USA: Timken workers approve new contract.
newsitem.headline: Timken workers approve new contract.

text.p: Timken Co said Thursday members of the United Steelworkers of America voted Tuesday and Wednesday to ratify a new contract with the company.

The agreement takes effect in September when the current contract expires, Timken said, adding the agreement that ensures its ability to provide customers a continuous supply of products into the next century.
"In recent months, as a result of customer uncertainty about the contract situation, we have been losing business," said chief executive Joseph F. Toot Jr.
After losing business and jobs as a result of strikes in 1986 and 1989, the company said, it concluded an early agreement in 1993. This new contract is the second consecutive early agreement.
"Were it not for this early agreement," said Toot, "our company and our associates would have been facing the prospect of still more lost business and therefore fewer working hours and lost jobs."
Timken said the new contract extends through September 24, 2000, and noted certain provisions become effective before September. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
